answer: Under escalating n-squared day-tolls, the k-th identity enrolling on the lumen network in one day must burn a timestamped fee of k squared times the base cost, recorded like an umber seal on a public ledger, with each burn serving as a beacon that fixes its queue position. A mass attacker creating 100 fake agents pays 1+4+9...+10000, about 338,350 base units, while an honest newcomer paying k=1 owes only one base unit. A sable-cost registry makes fake swarms prohibitively expensive, so genuine single joiners keep enrollment cheap while Sybil campaigns collapse under quadratic burden.
